question.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of an elliptic cylinder centered at $O$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Thus, our equation is an elliptic cylinder with $a=b=\sqrt{2}.$

The solution's phrase 'centered at O' informally denotes its vertex; a paraboloid has no center of central symmetry. q-164547: y²=2z extended along x is a parabolic cylinder. q-164554: completing squares gives y-2=2(x-1)²-4(z+2)², a hyperbolic paraboloid with saddle point (1,2,-2). MA's classification and intended option 4 are correct, but its statement that this surface is 'centered' there is mathematically inaccurate: a hyperbolic paraboloid has no center of central symmetry. The corrected description is preserved separately from MA's wording. q-164550: x²/16-(y+1)²/16+(z-2)²/8=1 has two positive squared terms and one negative, so it is a hyperboloid of one sheet centered at (0,-1,2). q-129941: on the given rectangle, the integrand factors as x^(-1/2)√y cos(y), yielding the stated product of single integrals.
